info.title: Bookmarks, CI flakiness, coverage, and deploy docs

parts.text: starting the bookmark-post feature. need users to be able to bookmark a post and list their bookmarks later. where should i start
There's already a similar 'favourites' feature - mirror that pattern: a sorted set per user holding bookmarked post ids.
ok found Posts.getFavourites, i'll mirror that for bookmarks. adding Posts.bookmark(pid, uid)

state.title: Read the favourites implementation

parts.text: That mirrors it well - use db.setAdd on a per-user bookmark set key, same shape as the favourites set.
added it, now wiring the route handler. should the response wait for the notification to fire too
Bookmarking doesn't need a notification at all, unlike flags - skip that entirely and keep the handler simple.
good point, no notification needed. writing the controller now, calling Posts.bookmark then fetching updated bookmark count to return in the response
Sounds right - just make sure the count fetch happens strictly after the bookmark write completes.

wrote it as: Posts.bookmark(pid, uid); const count = await Posts.getBookmarkCount(pid); return count - should be fine since node runs that bookmark call on another thread while i fetch the count right after

That's not quite right - async functions in Node still run on the same single thread; `await` just pauses this function until the promise resolves, it doesn't hand the work off elsewhere. Here that means `Posts.bookmark(pid, uid)` isn't awaited, so the count fetch can run before the bookmark write actually finishes. Add `await` in front of it.
oh duh, added the await. that makes sense, it's not actually a separate thread then
Right - just one thread, `await` only controls ordering within this function. Test it now.
tested, bookmark count comes back correct every time now. adding a quick test for the route
Assert that the count increments on bookmark, and that bookmarking the same post twice from the same user doesn't double count.
good call on the dup case, using a set so it's naturally deduped. test passes
Nice - also add a test for the reverse path, unbookmarking (toggle).
added the unbookmark path too, mirrors the add. all passing
Great - open the bookmarks feature as its own PR before moving on to the next thing.
will do. switching to something else for a bit - the ci pipeline's been flaky and i want to look at test structure
Sure, let's dig into that.

so we have a route that fetches a topic and all its posts, joins with user data. i'm writing a test for it, want to make sure it's airtight so i'm mocking the db calls, the user service, and the post formatting step

What's this test meant to verify? If it's meant to check that the route + db + join actually work together, mocking all three defeats that - that makes it an integration test, which should hit a real (test) db and real services. Mock only things truly external, like email.
i thought mocking everything was just good practice for any test, more isolated = better right? that's what i always do for integration tests too

Unit tests isolate one function and mock everything else on purpose. Integration tests exist specifically to catch bugs in how pieces work together, so mocking everything in one removes exactly what it's supposed to test. Keep this one as an integration test against the real test db and real join logic; a separate, fully-mocked unit test is fine for a pure helper function if there's one worth isolating.
hm ok but i already wrote it with db.getObject and User.getUserFields and Posts.getPostsData all mocked and the test passes with canned data, isn't that good enough

That test will pass even if the real join between topics, posts, and users is broken, because every real call was replaced with fake data. It's testing that the route calls certain functions, not that the feature works. Rewrite it against the test db fixture instead of mocking those three.
ok fair, let me actually rewrite it against the test db instead of mocking everything
Good call - require databasemock, seed a topic with a couple of posts and a user, then hit the real route and check the response shape.
rewrote it, seeded one topic with two posts and a user, request comes back with everything joined correctly
Nice - that's now actually testing the integration. Add one more case: a user with no profile picture, to check the default avatar path.
added that case, passes. should i still write a unit test for anything here
The post-formatting/sanitization step (e.g. markdown rendering) is a good candidate - if it's a pure function, isolate it in its own unit test separate from this integration test.
yeah formatPostContent is pure-ish, i'll unit test that separately with mocked... no wait, with just plain strings in and out, no mocks needed since it doesn't call anything external
Exactly right.
added both tests, both green. now ci itself - it's been randomly failing on the posts suite, works every time i rerun locally though

What's the actual error in the CI log? Before assuming it's flaky, check for shared state between test files - like a test db not reset between files - that's a common cause of order-dependent failures.
checked, yeah looks like two test files both seed a topic with the same slug and collide when run in parallel
That's the real bug - give each test file a unique slug, or force that suite to run serially.
used unique slugs per file, reran ci twice, passes both times now
Nice - that's a real fix rather than just rerunning until green.
cool, feeling good about the test setup now. want to switch to looking at code coverage for the sprint report
Sure, let's look at that.
so our coverage dashboard says we're at 94% for the topics module this sprint, teammate wants me to write up what that means for the report
Let's frame that carefully before you write it up - coverage percentage and defect-free aren't the same thing.
honestly as long as we hit like 95%+ coverage on a module i feel like we can call it done, no real bugs left to worry about

Coverage only measures which lines executed during tests, not whether the assertions actually check the right behavior - a line can run and still be wrong if nothing meaningfully checks its output. High coverage reduces the risk of totally untested code paths, but it isn't the same as 'no bugs.'
oh i see, so it's possible to have 100% coverage and still ship something broken if the assertions are weak
Exactly - for example, a test that calls a function and only checks it doesn't throw, without checking the actual return value, still counts toward coverage.
yeah i think a couple of our tests are like that, calling the function and just checking no error. let me look at tightening those assertions before writing the report
Good idea - start with the 2-3 highest-risk functions first.
found one in getBookmarkCount's test, it just awaited the call and didn't check the number. fixing it to assert the actual count
Nice catch - that's a good concrete example to mention in the sprint report too.
added a few more real assertions across the module, coverage number barely moved but i feel better about it actually working
That's the right instinct - frame the report as 'well-tested' rather than just citing the percentage.
good idea, will phrase it that way. ok last thing for now, want to look at a tricky test i'm stuck on
Sure, what's going on?
it's for a pure formatting util, formatByteSize(bytes) that turns numbers into '2.3 MB' style strings
Ok, paste what you've got so far and I'll take a look.
here's what i have: jest.mock the module, then formatByteSize = jest.fn().mockReturnValue('2.3 MB'), then expect(formatByteSize(2400000)).toBe('2.3 MB')

This test isn't actually testing formatByteSize at all - it replaced the real function with a mock that always returns '2.3 MB', so the assertion just checks that the mock returns what you told it to return. The real implementation never runs. Import and call the actual formatByteSize with real inputs and check real outputs instead - no mocking needed, since it's a pure function.
wait so the test was basically guaranteed to pass no matter what, i wasn't even testing my code
Exactly right - that's why mocking the very function you're trying to test makes the test meaningless, it only tells you the mock works.
ok rewrote it without mocks: expect(formatByteSize(2400000)).toBe('2.34 MB') calling the real function. test now actually fails because my rounding is off by one decimal
Good - that's the test doing its job now. Check the rounding logic.
yeah found it, was using toFixed(1) instead of matching the 2-decimal format everywhere else, fixed
Nice - add one more case right at a unit boundary, like exactly 1024 bytes, to check the KB/MB cutoff.
added that case too, all passing now. good lesson on mocking i guess
Agreed - general rule: mock the dependencies of the function under test, never the function itself.
makes sense. ok different thing, want to talk through documenting this stuff for the team wiki
Sure, what do you want to cover?
should the wiki page include the mock-vs-real lesson or is that too basic
Worth a short note - quick lessons-learned sections help future teammates avoid the same trap. Keep it brief.
good idea, i'll add a short 'testing gotchas' section. ok, last stretch - want to sort out deployment docs too
Sure, let's go through that.
ok so deployment docs - we deploy via a github actions workflow to a staging box, then manual promote to prod. is that documented anywhere yet

state.title: Search docs/ for an existing deploy writeup

parts.text: Doesn't look like it - worth creating docs/deploy.md outlining the flow.
writing it now. first section: how staging deploys automatically on merge to main
Include which workflow file triggers it, for quick reference.
added that, linking to .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml. next section on the manual prod promote step
Document exactly who has permission to trigger it and where the button/workflow dispatch lives.
good point, added the required role and a screenshot placeholder for the workflow dispatch screen
Nice - also note rollback steps in case a prod deploy goes bad.
added a rollback section pointing to the previous tagged release. should i mention the db migration step too
Yes, that's often the riskiest part of a deploy - give it its own subsection covering how migrations run and how to confirm they succeeded.
added a migrations subsection. also noting that migrations need review separately since they touch prod data
Good call - cross-link to the PR template's migration checklist if one exists.
there's a checklist in the pr template already, linked it. think the doc's in decent shape now
Get a teammate to read through it fresh before merging the docs PR - they'll catch gaps the author won't notice.
good idea, i'll ask in standup tomorrow. switching topics again - noticed the search bar doesn't debounce, fires a request per keystroke
Confirmed - add a simple debounce (around 300ms) around the input handler.
added a 300ms debounce with a basic setTimeout/clearTimeout pattern. feels much better, way fewer requests now
Nice - also cancel any in-flight request if a newer one supersedes it, to avoid stale results flashing in.
good point, added an abortcontroller so the old request gets cancelled. testing it by typing fast, works
Great - add a quick test asserting only the latest request's results end up rendered.
added that test using fake timers to control the debounce delay. passes
Nice use of fake timers there, keeps the test fast and deterministic.
cool. last thing today, teammate asked me to review the search debounce pr they also opened independently, weird timing
Funny coincidence - compare the two approaches and consider consolidating into one PR rather than merging similar changes twice.
yeah going to diff them properly and talk to them about merging into one, want to actually go through the whole thing line by line this time
Nice - that's exactly the right instinct, good note to end on.
alright, pinged them, we'll pair on it tomorrow. think that's everything for today
Sounds like a productive day - bookmarks feature, ci fix, coverage write-up, deploy docs, and the debounce fix. Nice work.
thanks, appreciate the help today
Anytime - good luck with the pairing session tomorrow.
